newsitem.title: USA: U.S. orange juice output seen on upward trend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. orange juice output seen on upward trend.

text.p: U.S. production of orange juice should increase during the next few years as maturing trees come into full production, the U.S. Department of Agriculture said in a report on the outlook for horticulture.
"Trees planted in Florida following the December 1989 freeze are now beginning to mature and bear fruit," it said.

The report also noted an increase in Florida's orange crop may also lead to a rise in the quantity of oranges sold for fresh market, especially navel oranges, temples and tangelos. Currently most of Florida's oranges are used for processing.
Increased Florida production prompted two major firms that process orange juice in Brazil to buy existing plants in Florida in 1996, USDA said.
"These companies invested in Florida in order to protect their shares of the U.S. orange juice market in the face of expanding Florida orange production," the report said
Overall U.S. exports of horticultural products are expected to rise five percent in fiscal year 1996/97 (October/September) to $10.5 billion or 19 percent of total agricultural exports.
USDA noted that 12 years ago, horticultural exports were valued at slightly less than $3 billion and accounted for 10 percent of agricultural exports.

The U.S. is however, a net importer with net trade favoring imports by about $2 billion, the report said. An improvement in the balance of trade for fruits and tree nuts was seen resulting in evenly matched imports and exports of horticultural products within the next 10 years.
